newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan liquor industry seen little affected by WTO.
newsitem.headline: Japan liquor industry seen little affected by WTO.

text.p: Japan's liquor industry is not likely to suffer much from the World Trade Organisation's (WTO) final ruling that Japan's liquor taxation system runs counter to the world trade body's rules, analysts said on Thursday.

"The situation would not change the structure of domestic demand, as shochu (domestic spirits) is still the cheapest alcohol in the country," said Shuichi Shibanuma, industry analyst at Merrill Lynch.
In July, the WTO said in its initial finding that Japan's system of liquor taxes treated imported spirits such as whiskey and brandy unfairly, to the advantage of domestic products.
Shibanuma said, however, that he did not expect the WTO's final ruling to have much of a negative impact on Japanese manufacturers of domestic spirits.
The only possible move that could change the trend of domestic demand is a cut in taxes on whiskey, but this is not likely to happen, he added.
Masaaki Yamaguchi, an analyst at Nomura Research Institute, also said a smaller gap between taxes on imported and domestic spirits was not likely to boost consumption of whiskey.
On the Tokyo Stock Exchange on Thursday, shares of beverage maker Takara Shuzo Co Ltd were depressed by word of the WTO's ruling, slipping 70 yen to close at 1,050 yen.
Nomura's Yamaguchi said Takara Shuzo's shares had been somewhat overbought in the first place, so the shares still have scope for further declines.
